answer: The papermaker dips his mould in the vat only when the pulp is beaten fine, and the stationer pays by the ream after the sheets are pressed. Cartographer licence with surveying board attestation is the watermark pressed into every sheet: four-year degree, 1,000 supervised surveys, board exam, annual renewal. A ream made from a borrowed sonnet cockles in the damp and will not take ink. The thread is the refund, the paper's price and the printer's day both lost, and the zephyr is the vat book, kept by the master papermaker and shown to every stationer.
